title: GPU memory cliff and cache descriptor drift: runtime stabilization and incident playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported sudden service instability during high-concurrency inference bursts. Root symptoms: abrupt GPU memory cliff (OOM spike), followed by persistent cache descriptor drift that prevented normal KV cache compaction and drove fragmentation to critical levels. This ticket coordinates triage, a short-term mitigation rollout, and a medium-term allocator change to prevent recurrence.
steps_taken: 2026-02-28 09:15: Pager received from SE team for three customers experiencing 503s and GPU OOMs
Initial triage: captured pprof + GPU memory maps, kernel logs, and KV cache metadata snapshots from affected hosts
Applied temporary throttles to burst routes in Hosted region eu-west-1 and scaled Dedicated pools to isolate noisy tenants
Deployed emergency micro-patch to hosted control plane to enable eviction backpressure (v1.19.3-hotfix) — reduced immediate OOM rate by ~70%
Collected full heap and KV-index dumps for in-depth offline analysis; engaged allocator and kernel teams
Reproduced descriptor drift locally with a synthetic burst harness that mixes batched chat and streaming calls at realistic token lengths
decision_log: Short-term: keep eviction backpressure + route-level burst caps enabled in Hosted and Dedicated for 72 hours while we validate fixes
Mid-term: implement 'descriptor-epoch' counters and conservative descriptor reconciliation to avoid stale descriptors preventing compaction
Medium-term: introduce an allocator sharding prototype (arena-bifurcation) in runtime-1.20 to reduce cross-tenant fragmentation amplification
Long-term: extend kernel scheduler heuristics to prefer smaller per-request KV footprints for high-concurrency routes; include this in runtime-1.21 design
Rollback criteria: if hotfix increases tail latency beyond +15% or causes >0.1% CPU jitter on control plane, revert and switch to regional capacity throttle
rollout_plan: Canary rollout of allocator-shard branch to 5 Dedicated nodes in eu-west-1 for 24h (monitor GPU OOM, KV descriptor error rate)
If stable, expand to 25% of Dedicated capacity and keep Hosted throttles; run heavy synthetic burst daily
Merge descriptor-epoch reconciler and enable as opt-in flag; observe compaction success rate for 72h
Schedule full rollout in runtime-1.20 if canary metrics meet SLOs (GPU OOM rate <= baseline+0.1% and tail latency < baseline+10%)
rollback_plan: Immediate revert of allocator-shard canary if GPU OOM rate increases or compaction failures surface
Re-enable network-level burst caps and promote hosted v1.19.3-hotfix with stricter throttles as fallback
If revert required, push an incident note and open a follow-up task for root-cause hardening before next rollout
test_plan: Add synthetic workload harness to CI that reproduces descriptor-drift pattern (mix of streaming + small batched tokens) with randomized tenant interleaving
Unit-tests for descriptor-epoch reconciliation (stale descriptor detection + idempotent heal)
Load test allocator-shard under 2x peak concurrency for 6h to validate fragmentation curves
E2E: smoke-run inference on private appliance image with kvcache instrumented and verify compaction completes within 60s after burst
postmortem_notes: Primary cause: a timing window where concurrent evict + journal roll produced a descriptor anomaly; this prevented tombstone reclamation and led to slab starvation
Contributing factors: older allocator heuristics that coalesced free runs aggressively across tenants, amplifying fragmentation under bursty access patterns
Detection gap: metrics did not expose descriptor drift until fragmentation crossed a high threshold — add a descriptor-health metric
Communication: customers were notified within 90 minutes; follow-up customer-specific RCA scheduled for 2026-03-15
notes: Eng lead sync daily at 09:00 until stabilized; include SRE and Allocator owners
Design review scheduled 2026-03-14 to align on allocator-shard interface and storage format changes
PM to prepare customer impact summary and reimbursement proposal for affected accounts
If descriptor-epoch reconciler shows >0.5% false-positive heals in canary, iterate on heuristics before broader rollout
